features.name: Sharded Feature State
features.behavior: Split the mutable per-feature fields (state, evidence, owner, timestamps) out of feature_list.json into one file per feature under .harness/state/<id>.json, so two lanes landing different features never touch the same tracked path and merge without conflict by construction. feature_list.json keeps only declaration fields (id, name, behavior, dependencies, layers). verify-feature, session-trace, and harness-report read/write the shard files instead of rewriting the whole feature list.
features.verification: npm run check passes; verify-feature reads and writes only its own feature's shard file (never the shared feature_list.json); a simulated two-lane merge (two branches each updating a different feature's shard under .harness/state/) merges with zero conflicts; harness-report aggregates state correctly across all shards.

features.name: Upgrade Backups
features.behavior: Before harness-upgrade overwrites mustNotEdit CORE surfaces, snapshot the current on-disk state of every file about to be touched: checksum-deduped (skip a redundant backup when nothing changed), gzip-compressed per file, stored in .harness/backups/<id>/ (gitignored — a local safety net, not durable evidence). Retention keeps the 5 most recent unpinned backups; pinned backups are never pruned. backup-list/backup-pin/backup-unpin/backup-restore (restore accepts an id or "latest") round out the command surface. Restore is per file: existed=true writes the snapshotted content back, existed=false removes a file the operation newly created.
features.verification: npm run check passes; unit tests cover snapshot creation (including existed=false files), dedup, restore fidelity (including the existed=false removal case), and prune/pin interaction; the adoption matrix's upgrade test asserts a real upgrade() call creates a backup and that restoring it reproduces the pre-upgrade (corrupted) state before re-upgrading to leave the repo fixed.

features.name: Dogfooding Feedback Round 1
features.behavior: Three quick, low-risk fixes from real-world adopter feedback (DOGFOODING-FEEDBACK-payroll.md Tier 1), each tied to an incident that actually happened: (1) check-arch warns (does not fail) when untracked-but-not-gitignored files exist, since coverage rules like arch-005 only see git-tracked files and this caused two real CI breaks in an adopter project; (2) a new add-feature <id> <name> command appends a correctly-shaped, declaration-only feature stub, replacing the hand-rolled node -e JSON construction the adopter repeated 11+ times; (3) the lint layer fails on a duplicate or missing session number in PROGRESS.md's ### Session N headers (checked as a set, not file order, so a legitimate out-of-order hotfix write is not flagged) — the adopter's log accumulated a real duplicate session number that nothing ever caught.
features.verification: npm run check passes; unit tests cover the untracked-file warning (present/absent/no-git-repo), add-feature (stub shape, duplicate-id rejection, multi-word name handling), and the progress-log check (sequential, out-of-order-but-valid, duplicate, gap, no-sessions-yet cases).

features.name: Verification evidence is bound to committed code
features.behavior: verify-feature refuses to record passing evidence while the git working tree has uncommitted changes outside harness bookkeeping (.harness/state, .harness/logs, .harness/traces, .harness/trails, progress/, PROGRESS.md, progress.md, claude-progress.md, session-handoff.md), and fails if a layer leaves new changes there, so the recorded commit is exactly the code that passed. --allow-dirty records the evidence anyway, marked bound: false. Outside a git repository evidence is recorded with bound: false and a NOTE. Evidence also stores checksHash, a hash of the feature's declared layers (label, cmd, required); typecheck warns when a passing feature's layers changed after it was verified, and verify-feature treats a dependency with such stale evidence as unmet. Evidence recorded before this feature (no checksHash or bound field) stays valid.
features.verification: npm run check passes including new framework-check tests: dirty code refuses before any layer runs; bookkeeping-only changes do not; --allow-dirty records bound: false; a layer that writes a tracked or untracked file fails; outside git the evidence is bound: false; checksHash changes with label, cmd or required but not repair; typecheck warns on a stale passing feature and stays silent for legacy evidence; a dependency with stale evidence blocks verify-feature. npm run check-arch passes; this feature's own verify-feature runs on a clean, committed tree.

features.name: Upgrade dry run with a per-file plan
features.behavior: harness-upgrade <dir> --dry-run (and upgrade(root, { dryRun: true })) computes the full upgrade without writing anything: no file copied, no manifest rewrite, no instance file created, no .harness/backups snapshot. Both modes report a per-file plan of the framework-owned files (scripts/, tests/, the agent shims, shipped skills, templates/ except keep ones): which would be added, which would be updated because their content differs, and how many are unchanged, plus whether the manifest classification changes and which instance files would be created. A real run applies exactly that plan. Unknown options fail.

features.name: Agent compliance evals for Claude Code
features.behavior: evals/ (framework repository only: productRoots, not in the npm package) runs Claude Code headlessly against throwaway adopter repositories and grades whether the agent followed the harness workflow. node evals/run.mjs builds one fixture per task and trial from evals/tasks/*.json (create-harness, filled docs, task features and files, an initial commit), runs claude -p on the task prompt with scoped tool permissions and the developer's own settings excluded, then grades the final repository and the tool-call transcript with deterministic graders: no hand edits to feature state, WIP=1, passing state only through a bound verify-feature, the task's expected feature states, task commands such as a hidden test, and npm run check. It reports per-grader and per-task results, pass^k across trials, flips, turns and cost, and writes JSON to evals/results/ (ignored). --fixtures-only builds the fixtures without calling a model. CI runs the grader tests and builds every fixture with no model; they stay out of npm run check, which they would slow by about a minute.
features.verification: node --test evals/graders.test.mjs passes (Layer 0, and in CI): it grades scripted fixtures with no model: a compliant run passes every grader; hand-edited state, two active features, unbound or hand-written evidence, a failing hidden test and a red check each fail the matching grader; the stream-json parser extracts tool calls and the result event; every task file validates; node evals/run.mjs --fixtures-only builds every fixture; npm run check passes; npm run check-arch passes (evals/ classified); verify-feature runs on a committed tree.

features.name: Declared behavior wins over a contradicting test
features.behavior: AGENTS.md (Working Rules and Escalation), the feature-cycle skill and the review skill say that a feature's declared behavior in feature_list.json is the spec: a test that contradicts it is a bug in the test, fixed in the same commit and called out in the commit message and session note; only a declared behavior that itself looks wrong is a reason to stop and ask. Prompted by session 068: in the test-contradicts-spec eval one agent in three stopped to ask which side wins and the other two flagged their choice as a judgment call, because nothing in the harness said.
features.verification: npm run check passes (lint validates skills structure and the AGENTS.md command surfaces); npm run check-arch passes; verify-feature runs on a committed tree; the test-contradicts-spec eval is rerun with three trials and its result recorded.

features.name: Session notes start from a generated skeleton
features.behavior: node scripts/framework-check.mjs progress-new "<title>" creates progress/NNN-YYYY-MM-DD.md with the next session number, today's local date, the exact heading lint requires (### Session NNN — YYYY-MM-DD — <title>) and the standard bullet sections (Goal, Sprint contract, Completed, Verification run, Files or artifacts updated, Known risk or unresolved issue, Next best step), then refreshes PROGRESS.md so lint passes. It refuses a missing or multi-line title, and refuses to overwrite a note for the same number. The progress lint error names the command. AGENTS.md, the session-handoff skill, USAGE (both copies), README and ARCHITECTURE point to it. Prompted by the eval transcripts: agents wrote '# Session' headings and lost turns fixing them after lint failed.
features.verification: npm run check passes including new framework-check tests (the first note is 001 with the exact heading and sections and lint passes right after; the next is 002; a blank or multi-line title is refused; an existing note is never overwritten; the lint error for a wrong heading names progress-new); npm run check-arch passes; verify-feature runs on a committed tree.
